verdict.rationale: Aider's docs say it automatically commits its own edits with descriptive commit messages and marks them with '(aider)' attribution, which covers staging and committing. Branch creation is only reachable by the user running raw git through the /git command, and nothing documents the agent opening pull requests. One community user criticizes commit-message quality, but that is a quality complaint, not a contradiction of the capability. missing for 10: agent-driven branch creation, pull request creation, independent corroboration of commit-message quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent stage changes, write commit messages, create branches, and open pull requests

citations.quote: Whenever aider edits a file, it commits those changes with a descriptive commit message.
If aider authored the changes in a commit, they will have “(aider)” appended to the git author and git committer name metadata.
`/git` will let you run raw git commands to do more complex management of your git history.
